en.name: Fresh soba noodles
en.summary: Fresh soba — raw or pre-boiled buckwheat noodles sold chilled — is a refrigerated product with nothing in common with the dried kind. A sealed commercial pack runs about 9 days at 10 °C or below; once opened, cook it within 1–2 days. Frozen it keeps 2 months. The printed date on your pack always wins.
en.pantry: Fresh soba is not a pantry food and must not be left out. It is a wet wheat-and-buckwheat dough, and the sealed packs keep as long as they do only because of what the factory did: a mild acid dip and rapid chilling to below 10 °C within half an hour of packing. None of that protects a pack sitting on a warm counter. Cooked soba is a wet starch like cooked rice, so cool it quickly and refrigerate it rather than letting a bowl of noodles stand around.
en.fridge: Keep it at 10 °C or below — the Japanese hygiene rule for chilled noodles — and colder is better, so the main body of a domestic fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) is ideal. A sealed, unopened commercial pack of boiled soba is typically specified at 9 days from production, which is a manufacturer's figure for an unopened acid-treated pack rather than a home-kitchen finding, so treat the printed date as the real limit. Once you open the pack the acidity and the low-oxygen atmosphere no longer protect it: cook within 1–2 days.
en.freezer: It keeps 2 months at −18 °C (0 °F), frozen in the sealed pack. Be realistic about what you are preserving: buckwheat aroma fades quickly whether the noodles are frozen or not, so frozen soba is a convenience rather than a way to keep it at its best. Boil it straight from frozen. Frozen food stays safe indefinitely at −18 °C; the two months are a quality figure borrowed from fresh pasta.
en.thawing: Do not thaw — drop the noodles straight from the freezer into boiling water. Thawed fresh soba goes slack and breaks up.
spoilage: A sour, alcoholic or fermented smell when the pack is opened.
A slimy or sticky coating on the noodles, beyond the usual starch.
Any mould spot inside the pack, including at the seal.
A pack that has puffed up, or noodles gone grey and tacky.
tips: Buy it last and get it home cold; this is a chilled product, not a dry one.
Go by the printed date rather than any general figure.
Cook opened packs within a day or two — the pack's protection is gone once it is open.
Rinse boiled soba in cold water and refrigerate promptly if you are not eating it at once.

faq.q: How long does fresh soba keep in the fridge?
faq.a: A sealed commercial pack is typically specified at about 9 days at 10 °C or below. Once opened, 1–2 days.
Yes, 2 months at −18 °C (0 °F) in the sealed pack. Boil it straight from frozen.

faq.q: Is fresh soba stored like dried soba?
faq.a: No. Dried soba is a cupboard staple for a couple of years; fresh soba is a refrigerated product measured in days.

zh.name: 生蕎麥麵
zh.summary: 生蕎麥麵——冷藏販售的生麵或已汆燙過的蕎麥麵——是冷藏品，和乾蕎麥麵毫無共通之處。市售未開封包裝大約 9 天，須保持 10 °C 以下；開封後 1～2 天內煮掉；冷凍 2 個月。包裝上印的日期永遠優先。
zh.pantry: 生蕎麥麵不是常溫食品，不能放在外面。它是含水的小麥與蕎麥麵團，市售包裝之所以能放那麼久，靠的是工廠做的事：輕度浸酸，並在包裝後半小時內急速冷卻到 10 °C 以下。這些對放在溫暖檯面上的一包麵完全沒有保護作用。煮好的蕎麥麵屬於含水澱粉，和熟飯同類，請快速降溫冷藏，不要讓一碗麵放著。
zh.fridge: 請保持 10 °C 以下——這是日本對冷藏麵類的衛生規範——而且愈冷愈好，所以家用冰箱冷藏室的 4 °C 是理想位置。市售未開封的熟蕎麥麵包裝，業者常訂為生產後 9 天，那是「未開封、經浸酸處理」的廠方規格，不是家庭廚房的研究結果，所以請把包裝上印的日期當成真正的上限。一旦拆封，酸度與低氧包裝就不再保護它：請在 1～2 天內煮掉。
zh.freezer: 維持密封包裝放 −18 °C，可放 2 個月。但要看清楚你在保存什麼：不管凍不凍，蕎麥的香氣都消散得快，所以冷凍是方便，而不是留住最佳狀態的方法。要吃時直接從冷凍下滾水。−18 °C 下安全性是無限期的；這兩個月是借自生鮮義大利麵的品質數字。
zh.thawing: 不要解凍——直接從冷凍丟進滾水。解凍過的生蕎麥麵會軟爛、容易斷。
spoilage: 拆封時聞到酸味、酒味或發酵味。
麵條表面黏滑，超出正常的澱粉感。
包裝內出現任何霉點，包括封口處。
包裝脹起來，或麵條轉灰、摸起來黏手。
tips: 最後才買、盡快冷藏；這是冷藏品不是乾貨。
以包裝日期為準，不要套用任何通則數字。
開封後一兩天內煮掉——包裝的保護在開封那一刻就沒了。
汆燙後用冷水沖，不馬上吃就立刻冷藏。

faq.q: 生蕎麥麵冷藏可以放多久？
faq.a: 市售未開封包裝常見規格是 10 °C 以下約 9 天。開封後 1～2 天。
可以，維持密封包裝在 −18 °C 下 2 個月。直接從冷凍下滾水煮。

faq.q: 生蕎麥麵和乾蕎麥麵保存方式一樣嗎？
faq.a: 不一樣。乾蕎麥麵是可以放兩年左右的櫥櫃常備品；生蕎麥麵是以天計算的冷藏品。
